obligation: E-ISAC notice of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident (low impact)
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a low impact BES Cyber System at Substation N, E, L, or H (NERC Glossary definition of Reportable Cyber Security Incident)
deadline: CIP-003-9 sets no fixed time; it requires the determination and then notification unless prohibited by law. Company target: within 1 hour of the determination (POL-03 4.4)
notify: E-ISAC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - low impact BES Cyber Systems at 4 substations (P03 G-024)
clock_starts: Determination that the incident is Reportable, approved by the CIP Senior Manager

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable incident or attempt to compromise involving high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems or their EACMS
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
notify: E-ISAC and CISA (NCCIC successor)
applies_at_this_tier: No today - CIP-008-6 applies only to high and medium impact systems (P03 G-043). Would apply to the ADMS load-shedding module if it goes live as designed (G-007)

obligation: DOE-417 Emergency Alert (cyber)
citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 2 and 3; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b) (15 U.S.C. 772(b)); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Criterion 2: a Reportable Cyber Security Incident. Criterion 3: a cyber event that is not a Reportable Cyber Security Incident but causes interruptions of electrical system operations (for example, unauthorized SCADA commands that open feeders)
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident (telephone notice to the DOE Operations Center is acceptable when operations are critical, followed by the written form)
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system; DOE Operations Center by phone as backup). The form lets the filer share it with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - electric utility. File directly unless the Balancing Authority files for the company (written agreement due 2026-11-30, POAM-016)
runbook: A; B if ransomware reaches OT or interrupts operations

obligation: DOE-417 Normal Report
trigger: Criterion 11: a cyber event that could potentially impact electric power system adequacy or reliability. Criterion 12: loss of electric service to more than 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more (and no Emergency Alert criterion applies)
deadline: Within 6 hours of the incident
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 265,000 meters, so a wide outage can meet criterion 12

obligation: DOE-417 update and final report
citation: Form DOE-417 instructions (Update Report; Final Report)
trigger: Significant new information after an Emergency Alert or Normal Report; every filed report
deadline: Update when significant information becomes available; final report (updated Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident unless an interim update has been provided
notify: DOE
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: NERC EOP-004-4 event report
citation: NERC EOP-004-4 R2 and Attachment 1 (Distribution Provider events)
trigger: Damage or destruction of a company Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action; physical threat or suspicious device or activity at a Facility; uncontrolled loss of 200 MW or more of firm load for 15 minutes or more resulting from a BES Emergency
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the event met a threshold or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC and the parties in the Operating Plan (Reliability Coordinator; law enforcement where relevant). A DOE-417 form may be used as the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the DP is a listed entity. A cyber intrusion is reported only if it causes one of these outcomes
clock_starts: Recognition that a threshold was met

obligation: Operational notice to the transmission owners, Balancing Authority, and Reliability Coordinator
citation: Interconnection and operating agreements (contract); regional operating procedures
trigger: Any event that affects protection at Substations N, E, L, or H, the 230 kV or 115 kV lines, or load served from the BES; any change to UFLS availability
deadline: Immediately by phone from the DCC
notify: Transmission Owner A or B control center; BA; RC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational, not a cyber reporting rule

obligation: Notice to Utility Services client utilities (contract)
citation: Utility Services client contracts (security incident clause)
trigger: A security incident that affects, or may affect, client customer data or client services in the CIS partitions, AMI client tenant, CIS export, or contact center
deadline: Within 48 hours of the company becoming aware (contract); keep each client updated at least daily
notify: Each affected client utility duty officer and contract manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 4 client utilities
runbook: B; A if client AMI or outage calls are affected

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to client utilities (statute)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a client utility (the company is the client's third-party agent)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; give the client everything it needs for its own notices. The 48-hour contract clause is stricter and governs
notify: Each affected client utility (a covered entity or governmental entity under 501.171)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies to the client utilities' customer data
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
owner: General Counsel with the Director of Utility Services

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example, name with SSN, driver license number, or bank account number with access code held in the CIS or CIS export; or portal user name with password)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; 15 more days only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days; law enforcement delay on written request; written no-harm determination sent to the Department within 30 days
notify: Affected Florida residents (mail or email; substitute notice if cost exceeds $250,000 or more than 500,000 people)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the company's own customers. For client utility customers, the client gives notice unless it asks the company to send notices as its agent (501.171(6)(b))
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
owner: Vice President of Customer Operations with General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. The 15-day good-cause extension does not apply to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the company's own customers; each client utility files for its own customers

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Affected customers who reside outside Florida (about 6% of residential accounts have out-of-state mailing addresses)
deadline: Varies by state; follow the breach counsel playbook (due 2026-11-30)
notify: Residents and state regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - multi-state customer base

obligation: Vendor breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example, the CIS vendor, AMI vendor, collection agency, or contact center platform vendor) discovers a breach of company customer data
deadline: Statute: within 10 days after determination. STD-03 contract target: within 24 hours
notify: The company (Vice President of Customer Operations)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - tracked through vendor contracts
owner: Procurement Manager (contract); Vice President of Customer Operations (response)

obligation: Identity theft response for affected customers
trigger: Stolen data could be used to open or take over utility accounts
deadline: Apply the Program response steps (heightened verification, account monitoring) from the time theft is suspected
notify: Affected customers (with the breach notice); consumer reporting agencies if furnished data must be corrected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered accounts

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
trigger: Any intrusion into OT; any ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable (company target: same day)
notify: CISA (report.cisa.gov or CISA Central); FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports response help and OFAC mitigation

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before hiring response vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($25 million limit, $500,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would likely be covered because it reports under DOE-417 and the NERC CIP standards

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05; Regulation S-K Item 106 (17 CFR 229.106) for annual disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining the incident is material
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held and has no registered securities

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (confirmed by the General Counsel, 2026-07-20)

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification
notify: CISA Central; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company operates no pipelines

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification
trigger: Cyber attack on a power reactor licensee's digital assets
deadline: 1 hour / 4 hours / 8 hours depending on event
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no NRC reactor license
